svg.title: BPL: tasks, ingredients, and obstacles
svg.desc: Three columns with four numbered tasks and an added finishing task, ten unique ingredient nodes, and eight unique obstacle nodes. Fifteen blue-gray arrows show task uses. Fourteen solid teal arrows improve obstacles; thirteen dashed orange arrows introduce or worsen them. Tasks 3 and 4 construct and sparsify each stage. Finish is an added closure outside the numbered notes. Ingredients run from 1 to 10 top to bottom. This explanation order is not an execution schedule.
svg.text: Task wording follows the notes; ingredients appear once, in order from 1 to 10.

g.title: Selective shortcutting instantiates the correction step; the global matrix-power argument remains a separate obligation.
Node splitting instantiates weight reduction while controlling active-node growth; it does not replace the global correctness argument.
The clever pointer scheme describes sparse destinations by paths relative to one current vertex.
Reversible navigation supplies inverse access and returns without stacking full vertex addresses.
Streamed arithmetic bounds the numerical information retained by suspended calls throughout the sequence.
Trial runs estimate column crowding, freeze the column multipliers, and restart selective shortcutting. This is the column sparsifier in the notes.
Vertex splitting is node splitting: it reduces large residual weights where shortcutting is suppressed, with controlled active-node growth.
Sampled trial runs estimate the density of substantial incoming entries using the same conditional sampling interface.
The sampled estimators inside trial runs need bounded row and incoming access and the associated conditional normalization.
Recursion-friendly sampling makes the nested estimates accurate while limiting averaging descriptions retained across the entire sequence.
A coherent seed prescribes vertex subsets; rates matched to entry size reduce O(16^i) substantial neighbors to constant expected sampled degree.
Row and incoming caps bound degree on every seed. Conditional normalization compensates for suppression for ideal inputs; estimated inputs introduce controlled bias.
Conditional averaging of paired accuracy improvements controls recursive error and retained averaging words. It does not itself enforce worst-case degree.
During recursive averaging, compress accumulated estimates and normalization signals, controlling representation size and distortion before final gates and normalization.
Enumerate the analyzed conditional seed space and select a median of the root estimates.
Substituting continuation equations reduces residual entries in destinations where correction is enabled.
Shortcutting can create additional incoming connections.
A shortcut can expose several later destinations in one row.
The inverse access of the original graph does not directly enumerate the new shortcut computations.
Distributing incoming weight among copies reduces individual edge weights where shortcutting is suppressed.
Copies introduce additional possible destinations, although the active-node increase is controlled.
Destination copies may keep the same predecessors, and active source copies can add predecessors; splitting is not a degree bound.
Sampling at a rate matched to entry size leaves few substantial sampled entries in expectation.
Replacing exact contributions by samples introduces fluctuations, and seed reuse correlates recursive estimates.
Using conditional mixing requires descriptions of averaging walks that a recursive implementation must retain or regenerate.
A single seeded estimate need not be accurate.
Incoming gates and caps bound the correction relations even on inaccurate seeds.
Row gates bound the outgoing support of completed sampled rows.
A pointwise incoming-degree bound limits how often a common right-factor error is charged, without assuming independence.
Smooth gates, ranks, and estimated normalizers create numerical subcomputations whose storage must be controlled.
Paired budgets cancel the common ideal sample; conditional mixing contracts the remaining fluctuations.
Walk length is charged to the decrease in accuracy budget, limiting data suspended across recursive calls.
Averages and differences of individually sparse sampled contributions can involve many destinations in the accumulated intermediate row.
The averages and differences must be numerically evaluated without storing all their intermediate values.
Compress the intermediate estimated row assembled during averaging into a shared default and a budget-bounded set of exceptions; control the effect on later gated and normalized computations.
Compression changes intermediate estimated values; its distortion must be controlled even when noise and overflow are correlated.
Short relative descriptions replace a full saved vertex identifier in each suspended caller.
Discarding the old full address makes restoration and inverse access an explicit requirement of the pointer scheme.
Contours of appropriate computation trees enumerate incoming computations and supply restoring inverse access.
Restoring excursions avoid retaining a separate full starting address.
Compute requested digits while limiting numerical bits retained in suspended calls; the precision-dependent storage bounds compose across the recursion.
Enumerating the analyzed conditional seed space and taking a median removes reliance on one fortunate seed.

svg.text: 15 task links + 27 signed effects. Ingredient order is explanatory; tasks 3 and 4 inherit task 2's evaluation machinery.
i = stage index. Expected degree, worst-case access bounds, and accuracy are distinct. Scope: SPACE(log n log log n).
